page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r9a.4xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9T25 processor operating at a clock speed of 2.7 GHz, delivering 16 dedicated virtual CPUs. The architecture is configured with 128.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include dedicated hardware accelerators or GPUs.

Networking and I/O infrastructure for the instance features a baseline network throughput of 12 Gbps. The instance does not include bundled local storage, requiring the attachment of remote block storage volumes for persistent data operations. Additionally, zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned directly by default, necessitating standard virtual private cloud elastic network configurations for external reachability.

With its 1:8 core-to-memory density, the instance offers cost-efficient scaling for compute setups that are constrained primarily by RAM capacity rather than processing core count. By allocating 128 GB across 16 vCPUs, operations avoid paying for unneeded processor capacity when hosting large in-memory footprints. Tradeoffs include the complete absence of local ephemeral scratch disks and hardware vector acceleration extensions reported in this profile, relying on network-attached storage for disk operations.

The ecs.r9a.4xlarge instance is suited for high-density transactional databases, distributed in-memory caches, enterprise resource planning applications, real-time analytics engines, and medium-scale data processing pipelines.
